Naomi / Ben — technical appendix below. Ill keep this tight for the customer doc.

1) Warm standby approach (sub-5m target)
- Image & model snapshot caching on each host (pre-pull during shoulder hours).
- Maintain a small pool of hot-warmed nodes (10% of committed slab) with models already loaded into GPU memory. These nodes can be promoted in <90s in ideal conditions; cross-region placement increases time.
- If Praxis requires guaranteed <5m always, we recommend a dedicated warm-standby reservation (extra 5% capacity) — cost trade-off shown in the matrix.

2) Burst scaling policy
- Trigger: queue depth or 95th-percentile latency breach for 2 consecutive minutes.
- Scale step: add up to 25% of committed capacity per step, with maximum of +50% in the plan window. Steps spaced by 60–120s to allow KV cache propagation.
- Eviction bands: best-effort > soft-burst > production (production pinned until forced).

3) Preemptible fallback & continuity SLOs
- When preemptible nodes reclaim, traffic routed to quantized model variant and/or replicated warm nodes in a separate availability slab.
- Continuity SLO proposal: 95% of in-flight requests served within SLO during the first 10 minutes post-eviction; automatic rollback to previous routing policy if errors >3% for 5m.

4) Observability & runbooks
- Per-burst dashboard (headroom, scale events, median warm-up, evictions).
- Alerting: notify Ops and Praxis contacts at 70% headroom and on first scale step.

Ill produce numbers (expected warm-up CDF, cost delta, sample billing entries) for the matrix.

— Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
